The '''2021–22 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team''' represented [[Georgetown University]] in the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Hoyas, led by fifth-year head coach [[Patrick Ewing]], were members of the [[Big East Conference]]. The Hoyas played their home games at [[Capital One Arena]] in [[Washington, D.C.]]

Despite having won the  [[2021 Big East men's basketball tournament]] and a highly ranked 2021–2022 recruiting class, the Hoyas had a historically bad season. Winning their last game on December 15 and posting a 6–25 record overall, they went winless in Big East competition, finishing in last place in the regular season with a record of 0–19, and lost in the first round of the [[2022 Big East men's basketball tournament]]. Georgetown's second-worst season by winning percentage, it set a school record for losses overall and a school and conference record for conference losses in a season, and it began a school-record losing streak that remained active at the end of the season. It was the first winless conference season in Georgetown history and the first last-place conference finish for the school in the combined history of the [[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|original Big East Conference of 1979–2013]] and the new Big East Conference founded in 2013. It was the only Georgetown team to finish in last place in conference play other than the  [[1934–35 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1934–1935 team]], which finished in last place in the [[Eastern Intercollegiate Conference]].

==Previous season==
Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], the [[2020–21 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Hoyas]] played a reduced non-conference schedule and had four conference games canceled during the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–2021 season]]. They posted a final record of 13–13, 7–9 in [[2020–21 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East play]], and finished in eighth place in the conference. In the [[2021 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]], they defeated [[2020–21 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]], [[2020–21 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]], and [[2020–21 Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball team|Seton Hall]] to advance to the tournament championship game. In the championship, they defeated [[2020–21 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]] for the school's first tournament championship since [[2007 Big East men's basketball tournament|2007]]. As a result, the Hoyas received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], their first [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] appearance since [[2014–15 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2015]]. As the No. 12 seed in the East region, they lost in the first round to [[2020–21 Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball team|Colorado]].

It marked the first time since [[2017–18 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2017]] that the Hoyas did not play in the annual competition between the two conferences.<ref>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2021/6/24/22548893/skipped-georgetown-hoyas-not-scheduled-for-2021-gavitt-tipoff-games-big-east-big-ten-patrick-ewing Whipple, "Skipped: Georgetown Not Scheduled for 2021 Gavitt Tipoff Games", Casual Hoya, June 24, 2021 Accessed 26 June 2021]</ref>

To increase attendance in the lower bowl of Capital One Arena — an oversized venue for most college basketball games — and overcome the television optics of many empty seats down close to the court, Georgetown introduced a new ticket strategy for 2021–2022. It made tickets for each of six lower-profile non-conference home games (against [[2021–22 Dartmouth Big Green men's basketball team|Dartmouth]], [[2021–22 American Eagles men's basketball team|American]], [[2021–22 Siena Saints men's basketball team|Siena]], [[2021–22 Longwood Lancers men's basketball team|Longwood]], [[2021–22 UMBC Retrievers men's basketball team|UMBC]], and [[2021–22 Howard Bison men's basketball team|Howard]]) free for season-ticket holders, but required them to actively opt in to attending each of the games; if they did not opt in to a given game, Georgetown reallocated their tickets to others who wanted to attend. Georgetown also allowed season-ticket holders who did opt in to those games to request an additional four free tickets. In addition, the school redistributed seats to help fill the lower bowl for the games, allowing some season-ticket holders and their guests to sit closer to the court than they otherwise would have.<ref>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2021/7/28/22597243/season-ticket-holders-georgetown-hoyas-new-plan-aims-to-redistribute-fill-lower-bowl-kente-one-arena Whipple, "Season tix: Georgetown's New Plan Aims to Redistribute, Fill Lower Bowl", Casual Hoya, July 28, 2021 Accessed 27 November 2021]</ref> Georgetown also made all tickets to the opening game against Dartmouth free to anyone who requested one, both to boost early-season attendance and celebrate the return of fans to home games after their absence during the 2020–2021 season due to the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2021/10/26/22746503/hoya-hoop-club-virtual-season-preview-free-georgetown-dartmouth-tickets-patrick-ewing Whipple, "Hoop Club: Virtual Season Preview, Free Georgetown Ticket Promos! (Updated)", Casual Hoya, October 27, 2021 Accessed 27 November 2021]</ref>

Georgetown released its 2020–2021 roster later than usual, leading to speculation that roster turmoil might already have struck the team. When the roster was released on October 15, Tre King was missing from it.<ref name=casualhoya20211022>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2021/10/22/22740696/transfer-portal-eku-transfer-tre-king-re-enters-portal-georgetown-hoyas-patrick-ewing-dismissal Whipple, "Transfer Portal: EKU Transfer Tre King Re-enters Portal", Casual Hoya, October 22, 2021 Accessed 20 November 2021]</ref> The school released a statement that day explaining that King "did not meet the conduct expectations of the University. He is not enrolled in classes and will not be on the Men's Basketball team."<ref name=preston20211109/> King was dismissed from the university on October 16.<ref>[https://www.hoyasaxa.com/sports/bball.htm Anonymous, "Tre King To Iowa State", hoyasaxa.com, December 1 ,2021 Accessed 1 December 2021]</ref> He re-entered the transfer portal on October 22,<ref name=casualhoya20211022/> and his transfer to [[2021–22 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team|Iowa State]] was announced on December 1.<ref>"Transfer: EKU Transfer Forward Tre King Headed to Iowa State", Casual Hoya, December 1, 2021, Accessed December 1, 2021.</ref>

In their annual preseason poll in October, the Big East's coaches picked the Hoyas to finish in 10th place in the 11-team conference,<ref name=preston20211109/> a slight improvement over their 11th-place selection a year earlier.<ref name=preston20211109/><ref>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/10/28/big-east-coaches-pick-georgetown-finish-last-patrick-ewing-says-thats-about-right/ Copeland, Kareem, Big East coaches pick Georgetown to finish last. Patrick Ewing says that's about right", ''The Washington Post'', October 28, 2020 Accessed March 20, 2021]</ref><ref>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/11/24/georgetown-basketball-season-preview/ Copeland, Kareem, "Georgetown basketball searching for a new identity after troubled year", ''The Washington Post'', November 24, 2020 Accessed March 10, 2021]</ref> The loss of Tre King was a blow, and the 2021–2022 squad was a young team, rebuilding from its offseason roster turnover and facing possible frontcourt weaknesses. Sports pundits did not have high hopes for Georgetown to return to the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] in [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022]] and expected the Hoyas to finish in the bottom half of the Big East.<ref>thebigbigeastblog.wordpress.com Madden, Paytrick, "Georgetown Preview: Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice?" The Big Big East Blog, September 15, 2021, Accessed November 21, 2021.</ref><ref>[https://georgetownvoice.com/2021/10/01/georgetown-mens-basketball-schedule-analysis/ Fischbeck, Thomas, "Georgetown men's basketball schedule highlighted by weekend home games vs. Villanova, Syracuse"], ''[[The Georgetown Voice]]'', October 1, 2021, Accessed November 21, 2021.</ref> However, if the Hoyas made a successful non-conference showing and demonstrated an ability to stand up to powerhouse teams in the Big East, a [[National Invitation Tournament]] bid in [[2022 National Invitation Tournament|2022]] seemed a reasonable possibility as the 2021–2022 season began.<ref>[https://bustingbrackets.com/2021/10/11/georgetown-basketball-2021-22-season-preview-outlook-hoyas/2/ Anderson, Jarren, "Georgetown Basketball: 2021-22 season preview and outlook for Hoyas: Projected starting lineup: 2021-22 season outlook", Busting Brackets, October 11, 2021 Accessed 21 November 2021.]</ref>

During the 2020–2021 season, the Big East Conference had postponed and attempted to reschedule any conference game that a team could not play due to [[COVID-19 pandemic]] issues. In the fall of 2021, the Big East Conference announced a new policy for the 2021–2022 season requiring any team which could not play a conference game on its originally scheduled date due to an insufficient number of available players, ''including'' as a result of COVID-19 exposure or infections, to forfeit the game, with a loss assigned to that team and a win assigned to its scheduled opponent, the win and loss also applying to the conference standings.<ref>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2021/12/21/22848115/report-georgetowns-covid-issues-cause-forfeit-to-providence-patrick-ewing-carey-harris-rice-aminu "Report: Georgetown's COVID Issues Cause Forfeit to Providence", Casual Hoya, December 21, 2021 Accessed 24 December 2021]</ref> The policy was intended to incentivize all Big East teams to be fully vaccinated against COVID-19 so as to avoid forfeiting games.<ref>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2021/12/22/22850292/forfeit-updates-on-covid-policies-for-big-east-conference-big-12-acc-big-west-georgetown-hoyas-ewing "Forfeit: Big East Reverses COVID Cancelation Policy (Updated 12/23)", Casual Hoya, December 23, 2021 Accessed 23 December 2021]</ref>

===Non-conference season===

With all tickets free to anyone who requested one, the Hoyas drew 8,641 fans — including former Georgetown and NBA great [[Dikembe Mutombo]], who saw his son Ryan make his collegiate debut — to their opener against [[2021–22 Dartmouth Big Green men's basketball team|Dartmouth]] on November 13, the first game of a three-game homestand at Capital One Arena. Kobe Clark, Collin Holloway, and Timothy Ighoefe all sat out the game with injuries — Ighoefe due to a possible [[concussion]] he had suffered in practice — and center Malcolm Wilson made the first start of his college career and only his 13th appearance in a college game.<ref name=copeland20211113/> Dartmouth guard Brendan Barry had a connection to Georgetown — his grandfather Jim Barry had been a standout forward on the Hoya teams of [[1962–63 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1962–1963]], [[1964–65 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1964–1965]], and [[1965–66 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1965–1966]]  — but it was only the third meeting of the teams, the first since [[1974–75 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|December 1974]], and the first in Washington.<ref name=bender20211112>[https://dartmouthsports.com/news/2021/11/12/mbb-headed-to-nations-capital-to-take-on-georgetown-211112.aspx Bender, Rick, "Men Headed to Nation's Capital to Take on Georgetown", Dartmouth Sports, November 12, 2021 Accessed 27 November 2021]</ref> Dartmouth had not had a winning season since 1998–1999 or an NCAA Tournament bid since [[1959 NCAA University Division basketball tournament|1959]], had not fielded a team during the 2020–2021 season due to the COVID-19 pandemic, was expected to finish near the bottom of the [[Ivy League]] in 2021–2022, and had lost its season opener by 16 points to a [[2021–22 Boston College Eagles men's basketball team|Boston College team]] expected to finish near the bottom of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]], and Georgetown was a {{frac|16|1|2}}-point favorite.<ref name=copeland20211113/><ref name=bender20211112/> However, Dartmouth found great success in penetrating the Hoya defense and then passing the ball out for open three-point shots, and made 16 of 38 three-pointers (42 percent) during the game.<ref name=copeland20211113/> The Big Green went on an 18–2 run in the first half to take a 28–10 lead, and although the Hoyas scored seven straight points late in the first half, the Big Green led 37–21 at halftime.<ref name=copeland20211113/> The Hoyas started the second half with a 14–0 run to close to 37–35,<ref name=copeland20211113/><ref name=playbyplay20211113>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/playbyplay/_/gameId/401371996 Dartmouth vs. Georgetown – Play-By-Play – November 13, 2021 – ESPN]</ref> but Dartmouth then went on an 11–5 run of its own to pull out to a 48–40 lead.<ref name=playbyplay20211113/> The Hoyas mounted another comeback, scoring the next 10 points, and took their only lead of the game at 50–48 with 10:56 left to play,<ref name=copeland20211113/><ref name=playbyplay20211113/> but they held it for only 16 seconds as Dartmouth responded with a decisive 18–3 run and won 69–60 in a shocking upset.<ref name=copeland20211113/> Georgetown's all-time record against Dartmouth fell to 1–2.<ref name=bender20211112/> Aminu Mohammed led the Hoyas with 17 points and Donald Carey scored 14.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401371996 Dartmouth vs. Georgetown – Box Score – November 13, 2021 – ESPN]</ref>

Three days later, Georgetown had a much better game against [[2021–22 American Eagles men's basketball team|American]] — a team which had played only 10 games in 2020–2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic — and broke open a four-point game in the second half with a 24–2 run on the way to a 79–57 victory, the Hoyas' 11th straight win over the Eagles.<ref name=stevens20211116>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/11/16/georgetown-easy-win-american/ Stevens, Patrick, "Georgetown rights the ship after a tough opening night with an easy win over American", ''The Washington Post'', November 16, 2021 Accessed 27 November 2021]</ref> Aminu Mohammed had a [[double-double]] with 14 points and 10 rebounds, Dante Harris scored 13, Donald Carey added 12, and Timothy Ighoefe returned to action, scoring six points and grabbing 11 rebounds.<ref name=stevens20211116/><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401371997 American vs. Georgetown – Box Score – November 16, 2021 – ESPN]</ref> The Hoyas improved their record to 2–1 on November 19 with an 18-point victory over winless [[2021–22 Siena Saints men's basketball team|Siena]] — a team which entering the game ranked 339th in Division I in scoring offense and tied for 320th in scoring defense — in which Kaiden Rice snapped out of his season-opening slump, shooting 7-for-10 from three-point range and scoring 23 points, while Carey added 20, Harris scored 14, and Mohammed finished with 11.<ref>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/11/19/georgetown-siena-graduate-transfers/ Copeland, Kareem, "Hoyas turn to a pair of experienced hands to take care of Siena", ''The Washington Post'', November 19, 2021 Accessed 27 November 2021]</ref>

Georgetown had planned to play in the 2020 [[Wooden Legacy]] tournament the previous season, but it was cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>[https://247sports.com/college/ucla/Article/UCLA-Basketball-Report-UCLA-to-Face-Seton-Hall-in-Wooden-Legacy-152694237/ Pierson, Tracy, "Report: UCLA to Face Seton Hall in Wooden Legacy", October 10, 2020 Accessed March 7, 2021]</ref><ref>[https://www2.kusports.com/weblogs/tale-tait/2020/oct/8/more-clues-about-what-the-2020-21-kansas/ Tait, Matt, "More clues about what the 2020-21 Kansas basketball schedule might look like", kusports.com, October 8, 2020 Accessed March 21, 2021]</ref><ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4231741/2020/10/26/espn-cancels-college-basketball-bubble-plans-in-orlando/ Anonymous, "ESPN cancels college basketball bubble plans in Orlando", ''The Athletic'', October 26, 2020 Accessed March 21, 2021]</ref> Instead, the Hoyas played in the 2021 edition of the Wooden Legacy, going on the road for the first time in the 2021–2022 season to play in the tournament at [[Anaheim Arena]] in [[Anaheim, California]]. An eight-team tournament from 2013 through 2019, the Wooden Legacy debuted a new four-team format in 2021, and Georgetown faced [[2021–22 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|San Diego State]] in the semifinals on [[Thanksgiving (United States)|Thanksgiving]] night. The Hoyas had met the Aztecs only once before, in [[1981–82 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|December 1981]]. Entering the game, the Aztecs were ranked only 342nd in Division I in three-point shooting at 24.6 percent while Georgetown was ranked 21st, making 41.5 percent of its three-pointers.<ref name=zeigler20211125>[https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2021-11-25/san-diego-state-sdsu-aztecs-basketball-georgetown-hoyas-wooden-legacy-tournament-anaheim-arena Zeigler, Mark, "Aztecs put it together against Georgetown, set up clash with USC", ''The San Diego Union-Tribune'', November 25, 2021 Accessed 27 November 2021]</ref> During the game, however, San Diego State shot 7-of-16 from beyond the arc (43.8 percent) while Georgetown made only four out of 20 (20 percent) three-point shots.<ref name=zeigler20211125/> The Aztecs [[Slam dunk|dunked]] five times on the Hoyas and built a 54–39 lead before the Hoyas closed to four points behind at 57–53 with {{frac|9|1|2}} minutes left to play, but from there San Diego State outscored Georgetown 16–3 and won 73–56.<ref name=zeigler20211125/> Missing their last 10 shots, the Hoyas shot only 35.1 percent for the game and had only six assists.<ref name=zeigler20211125/> Aminu Mohammed and Dante Harris between them scored Georgetown's first 19 points and were the only Hoyas to finish in double figures, Mohammed with 20 points and Harris with 19.<ref name=boxscore20211125>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401371994 Georgetown vs. San Diego State – Box Score – November 25, 2021 – ESPN]</ref> Donald Carey, Georgetown's leading scorer entering the game at 15.3 points per game,<ref name=zeigler20211125/> managed only four points, all on free throws,<ref name=boxscore20211125/> while Kaiden Rice shot 2-for-7 (28.5 percent) from three-point range and finished with eight points.<ref name=zeigler20211125/><ref name=boxscore20211125/> It was the Aztecs' sixth straight win against the Big East, the longest active streak in the [[United States]],<ref name=zeigler20211125/> and it evened the all-time record between the schools at 1–1.<ref name=zeigler20211125/>

The next day, San Diego State met [[2021–22 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]] in the tournament championship, while Georgetown was a {{frac|7|1|2}}-point favorite against [[2021–22 Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball team|Saint Joseph's]], a 2–3 team, in the third-place game. Although the Hoyas and Hawks had played annually from the [[1961–62 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1961–1962]] through [[1979–80 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1979–1980]] seasons, it was the first meeting of the teams since then. Saint Joseph's led 15–14 with 11 minutes left in the first half, but after the Hoyas scored to take a 16–15 lead, the Hawks went on a 12–0 run and pulled ahead 27–16.<ref name=casualhoya20211126>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2021/11/26/22804388/agony-in-anaheim-georgetown-hoyas-funked-in-the-wooden-legacy-tournament-falling-77-74-to-st-joes "Agony in Anaheim: Hoyas Funked in the Wooden Legacy Tournament, falling 77-74 to St. Joe's", Casual Hoya, Accessed 27 November 2021]</ref> Although Georgetown switched to an aggressive and effective full-court press and cut the lead to eight, the Hoyas shot only 30 percent from the field in the first half and at halftime Saint Joseph's led 36–26.<ref name=casualhoya20211126/> After halftime, a 7–0 Hoya run helped Georgetown close the gap, and the Hoyas eventually took a 54–53 lead.<ref name=casualhoya20211126/> Saint Joseph's responded with a 7–0 run of its own, and Georgetown again came back to close to 66–64. In the final seconds, Donald Carey lost the ball on a bad pass attempt with the Hawks leading 74–72, and Collin Holloway's last-second three-point attempt was blocked from behind, giving Saint Joseph's a 77–74 win.<ref name=casualhoya20211126/> Saint Joseph's senior forward Taylor Funk had an outstanding performance, scoring a game-high 29 points on 9-for-11 (82 percent) shooting, including 8-for-10 from three-point range, and grabbing seven rebounds.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401377135 Saint Joseph's vs. Georgetown – Game Recap – November 26, 2021 – ESPN]</ref> Kaiden Rice led the Hoyas with 25 points, while Dante Harris scored 17, Donald Carey finished with 12, and Timothy Ighoefe grabbed 14 rebounds and added four points.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401377135 Saint Joseph's vs. Georgetown – Box Score – November 26, 2021 – ESPN]</ref> The Hawks' victory tied the all-time series between the schools at 17–17<ref name=casualhoya20211126/> and dropped the Hoyas to 2–3 on the season. They returned to Washington ranked 230th in Division I in perimeter defense, allowing opponents to shoot 34.3 percent from three-point range.<ref name=copeland20211130>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/11/30/georgetown-longwood-basketball/ Copeland, Kareem, "Georgetown sputters early but finds its way to a 91-83 victory over Longwood", ''The Washington Post'', November 30, 2021 Accessed 5 December 2021.]</ref>

Georgetown next met [[2021–22 Longwood Lancers men's basketball team|Longwood]] before a sparse crowd at Capital One Arena.<ref name=copeland20211130/> Longwood had never beaten a major-conference team<ref name=copeland20211130/> but scored the first nine points of the game on three three-pointers and shot 40 percent from beyond the arc during the first half.<ref name=copeland20211130/> The Hoyas did not take their first lead until pulling ahead 28–27 with 3:56 left in the first half, then pulled away with a 12–4 run to end the half. Although Georgetown led for the rest of the game, the Lancers, who shot 37.5 percent from three-point range for the game, twice cut the deficit  to one point. Georgetown still led by only three points with under three minutes to play,<ref name=copeland20211130/> but then pulled ahead 81–75,<ref name=copeland20211130/> and Longwood never got closer than four points the rest of the way.<ref name=copeland20211130/> The Hoyas evened their record at 3–3 with a 91–83 victory.<ref name=copeland20211130/> Sophomore Collin Holloway, who scored a total of 15 points during his freshman year, came off the bench to lead the Hoyas with a career-high 23 points on 7-of-9 shooting from the field, while Aminu Mohammed had a double-double (15 points and 11 rebounds), Kaiden Rice finished with 15 points on five three-pointers, Dante Harris added 14 points, seven rebounds, and five assists, and Donald Carey scored 12 points.<ref name=copeland20211130/><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401371998 Longwood vs. Georgetown – Box Score – November 30, 2021 – ESPN]</ref> Timothy Ighoefe left the game in the first half with what turned out to be a broken hand; he did not return to the game<ref name=copeland20211130/> and had surgery on December 2, and on December 3 Ewing announced that he would be out of action for four to six weeks.<ref>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2021/12/3/22812335/big-tim-georgetown-center-timothy-ighoefe-out-broken-hand-ewing-mutombo-wilson-billingley-holloway "Big Tim: Georgetown Center Timothy Ighoefe Out with Broken Hand", Casual Hoya, December 3, 2021 Accessed 5 December 2021]</ref>

Georgetown went back on the road to meet [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]] on December 5 in the first year of a two-year home-and-home series against the Gamecocks.<ref>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2021/6/15/22535506/schedule-south-carolina-gamecocks-will-host-georgetown-hoyas-on-dec-5-as-part-of-home-and-home Whipple, "Schedule: South Carolina Will Host Georgetown as Part of Home-and-Home Deal", Casual Hoya, June 15, 2021 Accessed 20 June 2021]</ref> [[Tracy McGrady]], who had played and coached with Ewing in the NBA, South Carolina and NBA great [[Alex English]], and Dikembe Mutombo all attended the game.<ref name=zietlow20211205>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/12/05/georgetown-south-carolina/ Zietlow, Alex, "Georgetown December 5, 2021 Accessed 5 December 2021]</ref> Georgetown used a 14–4 run to close to 25–23, but South Carolina finished the half with an 11–4 spurt of its own, and Georgetown went into the locker room at halftime behind 36–27.<ref name=ap20211205/><ref name=casual20211205/> The Hoyas spent most of the second half trailing by about eight points,<ref name=zietlow20211205/> fell as many as 15 The homestand began with a blowout win over [[2021–22 UMBC Retrievers men's basketball team|UMBC]] in which Georgetown scored 100 points for the first time since [[2018–19 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|December 2018]] — and fourth time in Ewing's tenure as head coach — and improved its all-time record against the Retrievers to 5–0.<ref name=stevens20211208>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/12/08/georgetown-umbc-kaiden-rice-basketball/ Stevens, Patrick, "Georgetown handles UMBC as Kaiden Rice heats up for 34", ''The Washington Post'', December 8, 2021 Accessed 9 December 2021]</ref> Kaiden Rice bounced back from his ineffective outing against South Carolina three days earlier with an historic game, leading the Hoyas with a career-high 34 points<ref name=stevens20211208/> — the first Hoya to score 30 or more points in a game since [[Mac McClung]] in December 2018<ref name=stevens20211208/> — on 11-for-14 shooting from the field, and his 10 three-pointers (on 12 attempts)<ref name=stevens20211208/><ref name=recap20211208>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401371999 "Rice scores 34 to carry Georgetown over UMBC 100-71", Associated Press, December 8, 2021 Accessed 9 December 2021]</ref><ref the second half — broke the previous school record of seven in a single game, set by [[Mark Tillmon]] in [[1989–90 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1990]] and matched several times since.<ref name=stevens20211208/> With his father Dikembe again looking on, Ryan Mutombo had his first collegiate double-double with 15 points and 11 rebounds, both career highs,<ref name=stevens20211208/><ref name=recap20211208/><ref name=ap20211208/> while Aminu Mohammed finished with the third double-double (13 points and 10 rebounds) of his collegiate career.<ref name=stevens20211208/><ref name=recap20211208/><ref name=ap20211208/> Dante Harris added 13 points.<ref name=recap20211208/><ref name=ap20211208/>

In front of its largest crowd of the season by far — including former Georgetown and NBA greats Dikembe Mutombo and [[Alonzo Mourning]] and former [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] standout and NBA player [[Rony Seikaly]] — Georgetown next faced [[2021–22 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] on December 11,<ref name=wang20211211>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/12/11/georgetown-upsets-syracuse-ewing-boeheim/ Wang, Gene, "On a day filled with warm memories, Georgetown upends Syracuse to create a new one", ''The Washington Post'', December 11, 2021 Accessed 12 December 2021.]</ref> the 97th meeting of the schools in a series that dated to [[1929–30 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1930]].<ref name=wang20211211/> It was the annual renewal of [[Georgetown–Syracuse men's basketball rivalry|the archrivalry]] between the schools during their membership in the [[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|original Big East Conference]] of 1979–2013, when [[John Thompson (basketball)|John Thompson]] coached Georgetown and [[Jim Boeheim]] coached Syracuse. Thompson had died in 2020, and before the first game of the 2020–21 season, Georgetown had named its home court "John Thompson Jr. Court" in his honor in a ceremony at [[McDonough Gymnasium]], where Georgetown played all of its home games that season with no fans in the stands because of the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.<ref name=georgetownedu20201126>[https://www.georgetown.edu/news/georgetown-names-hoya-basketball-court-after-legendary-coach-john-thompson-jr/ Anonymous, "Georgetown Names Hoya Basketball Court After Legendary Coach John Thompson Jr.", Georgetown University, November 26, 2020 Accessed March 16, 2021]</ref> The school planned to dedicate the home court's name at Capital One Arena in front of fans when public health restrictions allowed a resumption of games there and with fans in attendance.<ref name=georgetownedu20201126/> Play resumed at Capital One Arena and fans returned to games at the beginning of the 2021–2022 season, but — although the name "John Thompson Jr. Court" appeared on the court at Capital One Arena from the first game of the season — Georgetown waited until a ceremony before the Syracuse game to dedicate the court, with Boeheim — in his 46th season as Syracuse's head coach — looking on with a smile.<ref name=wang20211211/>

Georgetown took the lead five minutes into the game on three straight Kaiden Rice three-pointers,<ref name=ap20211211>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401370004 Anonymous, "Mohammed leads Georgetown past Syracuse 79-75", Associated Press, December 11, 2021Accessed 12 December 2021]</ref> but Syracuse responded with a 9–0 run and the Orange retook the lead in the middle of the first half.<ref name=ap20211211/> Georgetown had trouble scoring against Syracuse's strong [[zone defense]] in the first half,<ref name=wang20211211/> shooting only 37 percent from the field to Syracuse's 56 percent, and at halftime trailed 44–34.<ref name=ap20211211/> Ewing went with a smaller, quicker lineup during the second half to overcome the Orange's zone defense, using a rotation of guards and forwards rather than relying on a post player handling the ball in the middle of the zone, resulting in the Hoyas shooting 56 percent from the field after halftime.<ref name=wang20211211/> Georgetown opened the second half with a 21–9 run,<ref name=ap20211211/> giving the Hoyas their first lead since the middle of the first half at 55–53 with {{frac|11|1|2}} minutes remaining in the game.<ref name=ap20211211/> All five Syracuse starters averaged in double figures on the season and scored in double figures during the game,<ref name=ap20211211/> but Georgetown's defense clamped down in the second half. Although the Orange's third-leading scorer and top three-point shooter, junior guard [[Joseph Girard III]], went 4-for-6 from the field in the first half, he did not score again until 10 seconds remained in the game thanks to Dante Harris's defense — and to that of Tyler Beard, who filled in for Harris when Harris departed the game for four minutes in the second half after hurting his ankle in a hard fall.<ref name=wang20211211/> During the second half, Syracuse shot only 36.1 percent from the field and 3-for-14 (21.4 percent) from three-point range.<ref name=wang20211211/> The Hoyas made their last six free throws,<ref name=wang20211211/> and Georgetown took the lead for good at 75–73 with 1:11 left to play<ref name=wang20211211/> on a Kaiden Rice three-pointer — his first three-pointer after seven straight misses.<ref name=ap20211211/> Georgetown committed 11 turnovers, seven of them in the second half, and Syracuse outscored the Hoyas 42–26 in the paint, but Georgetown attempted 10 more free throws than the Orange and outrebounded Syracuse 38–31,<ref name=wang20211211/> and Georgetown won 79–75.<ref name=wang20211211/><ref name=ap20211211/> Aminu Mohammed shot 7-for-14 from the field and sank eight out of nine free throws, scored 20 points in the second half, and finished with a double-double (a game-high and career-high 23 points and a game-high and career-high 13 rebounds) along with two blocked shots, two steals, and a personal-best five assists;<ref name=wang20211211/><ref name=ap20211211/> his two free throws with nine seconds left clinched the win.<ref name=ap20211211/> Donald Carey added 18 points on 4-for-7 shooting from beyond the arc and 6-for-6 from the free-throw line,<ref name=wang20211211/><ref name=ap20211211/> while Kaiden Rice made five of his 15 three-point attempts to finish with 15 points.<ref name=wang20211211/><ref name=ap20211211/> Off the bench, Collin Holloway scored 10 points, eight of them in the second half.<ref name=ap20211211/>

With Timothy Ighoefe still out of action, Jordan Riley out indefinitely with a shoulder injury suffered during the UMBC game that required surgery, and Jalin Billingsley and second-leading scorer Kaiden Rice (at 14.5 points per game on 43.3 percent three-point shooting) sidelined by a non-COVID-19-related illness, the Hoyas — with only seven scholarship players available — were shorthanded four days later when they hosted a [[2021–22 Howard Bison men's basketball team|Howard]] team that was much improved from its previous two seasons.<ref name=stevens20211215>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/12/15/georgetown-howard-college-basketball/ Stevens, Patrick, "Shorthanded Georgetown holds off Howard for third straight win", ''The Washington Post'', December 15, 2021 Accessed 16 December 2021]</ref> Bison fifth-year senior guard Kyle Foster scored a career-high 26 points during the game and Howard led 31–22 in the first half before the Hoyas took the lead for good with a 24–6 run before halftime.<ref name=stevens20211215/> Both Aminu Mohammed and Collin Holloway fouled out in the game's final minutes, leaving Georgetown with only five scholarship players available, so walk-on Chuma Azinge stepped in and logged a career-high nine minutes.<ref name=stevens20211215/> Howard got as close as 56–52 in the second half, but an 18–4 Hoya run followed that sealed the victory for Georgetown.<ref name=stevens20211215/> Georgetown's defense forced a season-high 21 turnovers.<ref name=ai20211215>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401372000 "Beard scores 23 to carry Georgetown over Howard 85-73", Automated Insights, December 15, 2021 Accessed 16 December 2021]</ref> It was the Hoyas' sixth straight home victory,<ref name=ai20211215/> and it improved Georgetown's all-time record against the Bison to 11–0<ref name=stevens20211215/> in a series that dated back to [[1999–2000 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1999]]. Tyler Beard, who had scored a total of 14 points in the previous nine games of his collegiate career, came off the bench for a career-high 23 points.<ref name=stevens20211215/><ref name=ai20211215/> Holloway scored 15 in his first collegiate start<ref name=stevens20211215/><ref name=ai20211215/> and Malcolm Wilson finished with a 13 points and eight rebounds — both career highs — and blocked four shots.<ref name=stevens20211215/><ref name=ai20211215/> Two other Hoyas also scored in double figures, with Donald Carey adding 14 points<ref name=ai20211215/> and Dante Harris 10.<ref name=stevens20211215/> The victory gave Georgetown a 49–0 record all-time against the eight programs that made up the [[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference]] at the time<ref name=stevens20211215/> and it extended the Hoyas' winning streak to three, the longest regular-season winning streak for Georgetown since [[2019–20 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|December 2019]].<ref name=copeland20211218>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/12/18/georgetown-tcu-basketball/ Copeland, Kareem, "Georgetown's three-game winning streak comes to an end against TCU", ''The Washington Post'', December 18, 2021 Accessed 19 December 2021]</ref> However, it also was Georgetown's last victory of the season.

What turned out to be a school-record losing streak began when Georgetown finished its non-conference schedule by hosting [[2021–22 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|TCU]] on December 18 in the final game of the annual [[Big East–Big 12 Alliance|Big East–Big 12 Battle]].<ref name=copeland20211218/><ref name=ap20211218/> It was the first meeting of the schools, and the first game TCU ever played in Washington, D.C.<ref name=ap20211218>[https://apnews.com/article/sports-mens-college-basketball-college-basketball-georgetown-hoyas-mens-basketball-dante-harris-b9b16c12f8d3e5719a5eb43385dfed5b Anonymous, "Miles sparks TCU to 80-73 win over Georgetown", Associated Press, December 18, 2021 Accessed 19 December 2021]</ref> Jalin Billingsley and Kaiden Rice returned to action, but Dante Harris was sidelined, having sprained his ankle in the Syracuse game and aggravated the injury during practice on December 17,<ref name=copeland20211218/><ref name=ap20211218/> leaving Tyler Beard to fill in for him at point guard. TCU jumped out to an early 10–4 lead, but Georgetown closed the gap and took the lead at 13–12 with 11 minutes left in the first half.<ref name=casual20211218>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2021/12/18/22844161/horned-depleted-hoyas-fall-narrowly-tcu-80-73-ewing-aminu-carey-rice-billingsley-mutombo-georgetown "HORNED: Depleted Hoyas Fall Narrowly to TCU, 80-73", Casual Hoya, December 18, 2021 Accessed 19 December 2021]</ref> TCU later jumped out to a 30–23 lead — the largest lead either team had in the first half — before the Hoyas scored nine straight points to pull ahead 32–30,<ref name=ap20211218/> and from there the two teams were unable to achieve much separation from one another; although TCU led for 26 minutes overall during the game<ref name=copeland20211218/> — never by double digits<ref name=copeland20211218/> — and Georgetown trailed 39–36 at halftime,<ref name=casual20211218/> there were 13 ties and 16 lead changes during the game.<ref name=ap20211218/> The second half was back-and-forth and Georgetown led 61–59 midway through the half, but then TCU went on a decisive 14–3 run that ended with 4:14 left to play put the Horned Frogs ahead 73–64, their largest lead of the game;<ref name=copeland20211218/><ref name=ap20211218/> although the Hoyas closed to 76–73,<ref name=ap20211218/> TCU scored the final four points to win 80–73, the Horned Frogs′ sixth straight victory.<ref name=copeland20211218/><ref name=ap20211218/> Aminu Mohammed had a double-double (game highs of 21 points and 11 rebounds), Kaiden Rice went 4-for-11 in three-pointers and scored 14 points, and Donald Carey added 12.<ref name=copeland20211218/><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401371995 TCU vs. Georgetown – Box Score – December 18, 2021 – ESPN]</ref> Georgetown's persistent weakness over several years in three-point defense<ref name=copeland20211218/> — the Hoyas were ranked 10th in the 11-team Big East in defending against three-pointers<ref name=copeland20211218/> — was on display, allowing the Horned Frogs to sink a season-high 11 three-pointers;<ref name=copeland20211218/> shooting 27.9 percent from beyond the arc entering the game, TCU sank 42 percent of its three-point shots against the Hoyas.<ref name=casual20211218/> Georgetown wrapped up the non-conference portion of its schedule with a record of 6–5.

===Conference season===

====COVID-19 pause====
The [[2020–21 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|previous season]], with [[2020–21 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|Connecticut]] joining the Big East, plans had called for Georgetown to play its first-ever 20-game Big East Conference schedule, with a home-and-home series against each of the other ten Big East teams, but cancellations due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] had reduced the Hoyas' conference schedule to 16 games.<ref name=copeland20211221>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/12/21/gerogetown-providence-forfeit/ Copeland, Kareem, "Georgetown forfeits game at Providence because of coronavirus issues", ''The Washington Post'', December 21, 2021 Accessed 22 December 2021]</ref> Plans again called for a 20-game conference schedule in 2021–2022, but COVID-19 again interfered. Under the new Big East Conference policy for the season, any team unable to field enough players for a game, including for COVID-19 reasons, was required to forfeit the game, and when COVID-19 problems arose on the Georgetown team after the conclusion of the non-conference schedule, the Hoyas were forced to forfeit their December 22 conference season opener at No. 22 [[2021–22 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]].<ref name=copeland20211221/> The forfeit temporarily dropped Georgetown's overall record to 6–6 and conference record to 0–1.<ref name=copeland20211221/>

On December 23, however, after four Big East games had been cancelled due to COVID-19 and with cases of the disease spiking across the United States, the Big East rescinded the policy requiring forfeits.<ref name=ap20211223>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/sec-big-east-alter-basketball-policies-as-covid-cases-spike/2021/12/23/1829e1ee-642d-11ec-9b51-7131fa190c5e_story.html Anonymous, "SEC, Big East alter basketball policies as COVID cases spike", Associated Press, December 23, 2021 Accessed 24 December 2021]</ref> It announced a new policy, under which a team would be required to play a scheduled game if it could field seven scholarship players and one "countable" coaching staff member for the game, but that no team would be required to forfeit a game it could not play for COVID-19 reasons.<ref name=ap20211223/><ref name=casual20211224>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2021/12/21/22848115/report-georgetowns-covid-issues-cause-forfeit-to-providence-patrick-ewing-carey-harris-rice-aminu "ANOTHER ONE: COVID Issues Cause Georgetown to Cancel Game at Creighton", Casual Hoya, December 24, 2021 Accessed 24 December 2021]</ref> Instead, any such game would be rescheduled if possible or declared a "no contest" if rescheduling proved impossible.<ref name=ap20211223/> The new policy erased Georgetown's forfeit to Providence and returned the team's record to 6–5 overall and 0–0 in the Big East. because of COVID-19 issues on the team.<ref name=casual20211224/> With continuing COVID-19 problems on both the Georgetown and [[2021–22 St. John's Red Storm men's basketball team|St. John's]] teams, The Hoyas next visited No. 21 [[2021–22 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]] — their first Top-25 opponent of the season — in a game rescheduled from December 22. It was Providence's first game in 12 days due to COVID-19-related cancellations.<ref name=espnrecap20220120>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401400491 Anonymous, "Croswell, Horchler lead No. 21 Providence over Georgetown," Associated Press, January 20, 2022]</ref> The Hoyas started slow, missing their first 11 shots and committing five turnovers in the first seven minutes, and the Friars opened a 13–0 lead before Georgetown scored.<ref name=scandula20220120>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2022/01/20/georgetown-providence-patrick-ewing-defense/ Scandula, Mike, "Georgetown’s Big East struggles continue with loss at No. 21 Providence," washingtonpost.com, Accessed 20 May 2022]</ref> Georgetown used an 18–2 run to close the gap<ref name=scandula20220120/> and trailed by only three points, 37–34, at halftime.<ref name=espnrecap20220120/> Providence opened the second half with an 11–2 run to take a 12-point lead,<ref name=scandula20220120/> and Georgetown fell behind by 16 points halfway through the second half before closing to a 64–60 deficit with five minutes remaining.<ref name=espnrecap20220120/><ref name=scandula20220120/> The Hoyas got no closer,<ref name=scandula20220120/> and the Friars held on to win 83–75,<ref name=espnrecap20220120/> giving Georgetown its first 0–4 conference start since 2016–2017. game,<ref name=espnrecap20220203/> and Dante Harris scored 12 against Seton Hall<ref name=espnboxscore20220201>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401373572 Seton Hall vs. The Hoyas finished the homestand by hosting Providence, which had risen to No. 15 in the [[Associated Press poll|AP poll]] and entered the game on a six-game winning streak.<ref name=espnrecap20220206>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401373580 Anonymous, "Bynum, Providence win; Hoyas drop school-worst 11th straight," Associated Press, February 6, 2022]</ref> It was the 1,500th broadcast — well over half the 2,803 Georgetown games ever played<ref>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2022/2/6/22919752/oh-my-rich-chvotkin-hits-1500-games Bancroft, Bobby, "OH MY: Rich Chvotkin Hits 1,500 games," Casual Hoya, February 6, 2022 Accessed 30 May 2022]</ref> — for longtime Georgetown radio voice Rich Chvotkin, who had broadcast every Georgetown game since the [[1974–75 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1974–1975 season]] except for missing most of the [[1990–91 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1990–1991 season]] while on [[United States Army Reserve]] duty during the [[Gulf War]].<ref name=espnrecap20220206/> The Hoyas forced Providence — which entered the game  averaging 11.8 turnovers per game<ref name=espnrecap20220206/> — into 10 turnovers in the first half<ref name=espnrecap20220206/> and led at halftime 30–27<ref name=espnrecap20220206/> despite committing nine turnovers of their own.<ref name=espnrecap20220206/> It was only the second halftime lead of the season against a Big East opponent for Georgetown,<ref name=espnrecap20220206/> but the tide turned after halftime. Georgetown scored only two field goals in the first 12:26 of the second half,<ref name=espnrecap20220206/> allowing Providence to take the lead and pull away. Friars junior guard Jared Bynum scored only five points in the first half,<ref name=espnrecap20220206/> but in the second half had a personal 13–0 run<ref name=espnrecap20220206/> and outscored the entire Georgetown team 27–22<ref name=espnrecap20220206/> to finish with a career-high 32 points.<ref name=espnrecap20220206/> Aminu Mohammed led the Hoyas with 18 points,<ref name=espnrecap20220206/><ref name=espnboxscore20220206>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401373580 Providence vs. Georgetown – Box Score – February 6, 2022 – ESPN]</ref> and Donald Carey scored 11,<ref name=espnboxscore20220206/> but the Friars won 71–52 in Providence's 12th victory in 15 games against Georgetown since [[2014–15 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2015]],<ref name=espnrecap20220206/> completing the Friars′ sixth regular-season sweep of the Hoyas in eight seasons.<ref name=espnrecap20220206/> The loss also extended the Hoyas′ losing streak to a school-record 11 games,<ref name=espnrecap20220206/> exceeding the 10-game skid that extended across the last nine games of the [[2003–04 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2003–2004 season]] and the opening game of the [[2004–05 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2004–2005 season]]. At 6–15, the Hoyas also fell to nine games below .500 for the first time since the [[1971–72 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1971–1972 season]], when they had posted a 3–23 record.<ref name=espnrecap20220206/>

The losing streak reached 12 games in a visit to [[2021–22 DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball team|DePaul]] in which Blue Demons sophomore forward David Jones had the first [[triple double]] in DePaul history (22 points, 14 rebounds, 10 assists).<ref name=espnrecap20220209>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401373585 Georgetown vs. DePaul – Game Recap – February 9, 2022 – ESPN]</ref> The Hoyas led 31–30 at halftime,<ref name=espnrecap20220209/> but the Blue Demons broke a second-half tie to put the game away with a 26–0 run as part of stretch in which they outscored the Hoyas 33–2.<ref name=espnrecap20220209/> A scheduling anomaly followed in which Georgetown played back-to-back games against [[2021–22 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]], caused by the rescheduling of the December 28 game at Creighton to February 14. name=espnrecap20220214>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401400492 Georgetown vs. Creighton – Game Recap – February 14, 2022 – ESPN]</ref> Kaiden Rice led the Hoyas with 24 points against DePaul<ref name=espnrecap20220209/> and scored 16 points in the first Creighton game.<ref name=espnrecap20220212/> Aminu Mohammed had a double-double (16 points and 10 rebounds) against Georgetown next visited No. 10 Villanova, the winner of four in a row, in the 91st meeting of the teams.<ref name=espnrecap20220219>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401373598 Anonymous, "Moore leads No. 10 Villanova to 74-66 win over Georgetown," Associated Press, February 19, 2022]</ref> Georgetown fell behind 16–5 in the first {{frac|10|1|2}} minutes, but the Hoyas took advantage of poor Villanova outside shooting to close to 19–18 with 4:14 left in the first half.<ref name=espnrecap20220219/> Villanova then finished the half with a 13–4 run.<ref name=espnrecap20220219/> The Hoyas held Villanova's two top scorers — guards Collin Gillespie and [[Justin Moore (basketball)|Justin Moore]] — to 13-of-15 (13.3 percent) shooting from the field in the opening half,<ref name=espnrecap20220219/> but themselves shot only 8-for-29 (27.6 percent) from the field and 3-of-14 (21.4 percent) in three-pointers,<ref name=espnrecap20220219/> and Georgetown trailed 32–22 at halftime.<ref name=espnrecap20220219/> Georgetown scored on two three-pointers to open the second half, cutting the Wildcats' lead to four.<ref name=espnrecap20220219/> As the half continued, the Hoyas twice closed to a three-point deficit, including an 11–3 run that made the score 56–53 with 8:22 left to play, but Villanova then had a 10–4 run to pull ahead 66–57 with 4:19 remaining.<ref name=espnrecap20220219/> The Wildcats went on to win 74–66, giving them a 46–45 edge in the series all-time,<ref name=espnrecap20220219/> Villanova's first series lead since 7–6 in 1976.<ref name=bancroft20220122/> Donald Carey scored 24 points<ref name=espnrecap20220219/> and Dante Harris added 16.<ref name=espnrecap20220219/> The loss dropped Patrick Ewing's record as head coach against Big East opponents to 26–59.<ref name=espnrecap20220219/>

After five days off, Georgetown opened its final homestand of the year by hosting DePaul, which snapped a four-game losing streak and handed the Hoyas their 17th straight defeat by scoring on a layup and two free throws in the final 59 seconds for a 68–65 victory.<ref name=espnrecap20220224>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401373605 DePaul vs. Georgetown – Game Recap – February 24, 2022 – ESPN]</ref> Aminu Mohammed just missed a double-double with 17 points and nine rebounds,<ref name=espnrecap20220224/> while Donald Carey scored 15 points and Jalin Billingsley 10 against the Blue Demons.<ref name=espnrecap20220224/> Georgetown then closed out its home season on February 27 with its final Top-25 opponent of the year, No. 21 Connecticut, which had a four-game winning streak entering the game.<ref name=espnrecap20220227>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401373609 Anonymous, "No. 21 UConn sends Hoyas to school-record 18th loss in row," Associated Press, February 27, 2022]</ref> The Huskies made 11 of 20 three-pointers against the Hoya defense, with seven different UConn players sinking at least one three-point shot.<ref name=espnrecap20220227/> UConn led 41–26 at halftime,<ref name=espnrecap20220227/> 66–46 with 11:27 remaining,<ref name=espnrecap20220227/> and 81–59 with 2:53 left play.<ref name=espnrecap20220227/> name=espnrecap20220227/> The loss concluded a winless February for the Hoyas, clinched a last-place conference finish for Georgetown for the first time in the combined history of the [[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|original Big East Conference of 1979–2013]] and the new Big East Conference,<ref name=espnrecap20220227/> and dropped Patrick Ewing's career head-coaching record to 68–81.<ref name=espnrecap20220227/>

In the immediate aftermath of the loss to Connecticut, the press asked Ewing about whether his job as head coach was secure, given the team's lack of success during the season, and he replied "Of course I want to be back here...But in this position and this job, whatever happens will happen. I’m hoping that I’ll be back and doing something that I love at a place that I love and getting us back to being the king of the hill."<ref name=fendrich20220302>[https://apnews.com/article/sports-college-sports-basketball-march-madness-mens-college-basketball-37b167070f6fda89f3c3bf609238f70c Fendrich, Howard, "Patrick Ewing gets statement of support from Georgetown AD," Associated Press, March 2, 2022]</ref> On March 2, Georgetown University athletic director Lee Reed issued a public statement in support o Ewing, acknowledging the "disappointment of a difficult season," but continuing: "In this ever[-]evolving landscape of college athletics we are committed to Coach Ewing, and we are working with him to evaluate every aspect of the men’s basketball program and to make the necessary changes for him to put us back on the path to success for next year."<ref name=fendrich20220302/>

Georgetown closed out the regular season with two road games. In the first, held the evening of March 2 not long after Reed's statement that day, the Hoyas lost to Seton Hall, with Kaiden Rice leading the team with 17 points, Collin Holloway adding 16, Dante Harris finishing with 12,<ref name=espnrecap20220302>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401373609 Georgetown vs. Seton Hall – Game Recap – March 2, 2022 – ESPN]</ref> and Donald Carey scoring 11.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401373613 Georgetown vs. Seton Hall – Box Score – March 2, 2022 – ESPN]</ref> Combining results in both the original Big East Conference of 1979–2013 and those of the Big East Conference formed in 2013, the loss tied the Big East record for losses in a season, matched only by 0–18 records posted by [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]] in [[1993–1994 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|the 1993–1994 season]] and [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]] in [[2009–09 DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball team|the 2008–2009 season]],<ref name=fendrich20220302/> during both of which Big East teams played 18-game conference schedules. In the season finale at [[2021–22 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]] three days later, the Musketeers broke a five-game losing streak to hand Georgetown its 20th loss overall and 19th conference loss in a row,<ref name=espnrecap20220305>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401373619 Georgetown vs. Xavier – Game Recap – March 5, 2022 – ESPN]</ref> setting a record for conference losses in a season by a Big East team. Dante Harris had 19 points, Collin Holloway added 17 points, and Aminu Mohammed finished with a double-double (15 points and 16 rebounds).<ref name=espnrecap20220305/>

Georgetown became the first Big East team ever to post an 0–19 record in regular-season conference play and only the third to have a winless conference season. The loss to Xavier completed the first winless conference season in school history. It also was the first time Georgetown has finished in last place in Big East history,<ref>{{Cite news |title=Georgetown's season ends in a 57-53 loss to Seton Hall in the Big East tournament |language=en-US |work=Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2022/03/10/georgetowns-season-ends-57-53-loss-seton-hall-big-east-tournament/ |access-date=2022-03-16 |issn=0190-8286}}</ref> and Georgetown's only last-place finish in a conference other than in [[1934–35 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|the 1934–1935 season]], when the Hoyas finished last in the [[Eastern Intercollegiate Conference]].

===Big East tournament===

Seeded 11th in the  [[2022 Big East men's basketball tournament|2022 Big East tournament]], Georgetown met the sixth seed, Seton Hall, in the first round at [[Madison Square Garden]] in [[New York City]] on March 9. After the Pirates scored the first four points of the game, the Hoyas took the lead with a 13–0 run to hold a 13–4 lead with 14:19 to play in the first half,<ref name=guhoyasrecap20220309>[https://guhoyas.com/news/2022/3/10/mens-basketball-georgetown-falls-to-seton-hall-in-big-east-first-round.aspx Anonymous, "Georgetown Falls to Seton Hall in BIG EAST First Round," guhoyas.com, March 9, 2022]</ref> Although Seton Hall clawed back, a 6–0 Hoya run gave Georgetown a 24–15 with 5:46 left in the half.<ref name=guhoyasrecap20220309/> The Hoyas led by as many as 10 points before Seton Hall whittled down the lead, and the Hoyas led 27–24 at halftime.<ref name=guhoyasrecap20220309/> In the second half, Georgetown led 37–33  with 15:04 left to play, 46–42 with 7:03 left, and 53–52 with 1:05 remaining in the game.<ref name=guhoyasrecap20220309/> The Hoyas did not score again, however, while Seton Hall scored five points in the final minute to win 57–53,<ref name=guhoyasrecap20220309/> bringing Georgetown's season to an end.<ref name=espnrecap20220309>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401403370 Georgetown vs. Seton Hall – Game Recap – March 9, 2022 – ESPN]</ref> Playing in their last game as Hoyas, Aminu Mohammed had a double-double with 12 points and 10 rebounds, Donald Carey and Collin Holloway each scored 11 points,<ref name=espnrecap20220309/> and Timothy Ighoefe grabbed 13 rebounds and had a career-high four blocks. Georgetown finished the season with an overall record of 6–25. It was the greatest number of losses ever suffered by Georgetown in a single season, and the team's .194 winning percentage was the second-worst in school history, with only the .115 winning percentage of [[1971–72 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|the 1971–1972 team]] ranking lower.
